rv.q: Searingly funny and incisively acted, the Second Stage Theater production shows that psychological terror can assume the most mundane form, and that the individuals with whom we share both DNA and personal memories still can be mysterious strangers.
Its humor and heart speak to the complexity of belonging to a family.
The Visitors does at least disabuse its overwhelmingly Western, undeniably progressive audience of the illusion of choice.

Director Jenna Worsham, who collaborated with the author a few years back on the well-received “At the Wedding,” has recruited fine actors who make the characters consistently engaging, even when their actions become frustrating or challenge credibility.
The good play and worthy performances would benefit from another visual concept or a more accommodating theater.
There’s an honesty to Turner’s characterizations in The Visitors, and a genuine humor, that justify spending time with this fractured family.

cn.t: Turner's family dramedy about siblings reuniting over a medical crisis earns praise for strong performances and sharp writing, though some find it conventional. Critics highlight its searingly funny moments and relatable dynamics.
